newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: EU MAY COMPENSATE S.AFRICA NEIGHBOURS - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: EU MAY COMPENSATE S.AFRICA NEIGHBOURS - PAPER.

text.p: The European Union has indicated the 15-nation trading bloc could compensate South Africa's neighbours who could be affected negatively by the proposed free trade area between the EU and South Africa, Business Day newspaper reported on Monday.

Joao de Deus Pinheiro, the EU commissioner in charge of relations with South Africa, hinted at the weekend the union could help out the Southern African Customs Union countries -- Botswana, Lesotho, Swaziland and Namibia -- with transitional measures and support joint ventures in the customs union using South African capital, the paper said.
However, he did not elaborate on the nature and scale of these transitional measures.

South Africa is in negotiations with the EU on a free trade deal, but the talks have been troubled by concerns from southern African countries that such an agreement could lead to a reduction of their customs revenue.

Business Day said the Lome Convention, the trade, political and aid accord between the EU and African countries, including the customs union signatories, but not South Africa, has a financial facility to help cushion countries from pain of structural adjustment programmes.
The paper said no decision had yet been taken on additional mechanisms to be used in coping with revenue loss which would result from the conclusion of the free trade accord.
